doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Learning bebop from records and his A&T thesis
summary: He learned Parker solos and the standards beneath bebop tunes, and wrote a thesis on the transition from swing to bebop.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Was learning bebop a matter of getting all the Charlie Parker records and learning the solos...

That’s right. Learning the solos and learning the standards that they came from. Most of those tunes came from standards. They just put another figure on the chords, and that’s how they played them. In fact, I wrote a thesis down there at North Carolina A&T, for my graduation thesis, and they took it and book-binded it and made it a book, and now all the students who go through the college have to study my book.
What’s the name of the thesis?
The Transition From Swing To Bebop.
Oh yeah. I got illustrations and chords, broke down the chords and everything. 1947.
Oh, yeah. And critical. Analytical and critical. So I was in good shape.
